newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber looking for further Thai buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber looking for further Thai buying.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was on the lookout on Thursday for further signs of buying by the Thai government while Malaysia was said to have sold about 500 tonnes of SMR20 rubber to China, dealers said.
A holiday in Japan put a dampener on sentiment in slow trading conditions in the local market by the midday break, they said.

"We're checking if the Thai government will come in again," a dealer for a North American rubber trading company said, refering to the purchase yesterday by Bangkok of 5,000 tonnes of RSS3 rubber in a bid to prop up sagging prices.
"I heard some Malaysian exporters sold about 400-500 tonnes of SMR20 rubber at about 287-288 Malaysian cents (a kg) FOB Malaysia (ports)," a dealer said.
Another trader said the modest buying seen in the market this morning has not helped the local exchange. "There was not much done this morning. It's just quiet," she said.

At around 0445 GMT, May RSS3 was indicated at 121.75 U.S. cents a kg from 122.00 cents. May RSS1 was indicated at 174.50 Singapore cents (US$1.22) a kg from 175.25 cents. May TSR20 was indicated at 162.50 Singapore cents ($1.13) a kg from 163.50 cents. - (US$1-S$1.43) - Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
